??? question "Which compiler stage works out the type of every expression and checks that operations, calls and returns fit together?"

    Type checking. For example, it rejects `3.0 & 1.0`, because bitwise operators need integers.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What is it called when overflow is handled by silently dropping the high bits, and does v0.1 do it?"

    Wrapping. Vortex v0.1 does not do it.

    Introduced in [9. Runtime safety](stage-9-runtime-safety.md).

??? question "What do we call storing a two-dimensional array one whole row after another?"

    Row-major order. Neighbours in a row are then neighbours in memory.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "What do we call storing a two-dimensional array one whole column after another?"

    Column-major order. Neighbours in a column are then neighbours in memory.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "What do we call how many bytes a value takes up, and what is it for an `f32`?"

    Its size. An `f32` takes four bytes.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "What do we call one trip over the whole program by one part of the compiler, doing one job?"

    A pass, such as checking types or lowering to IR.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What check makes sure `values[index]` stays inside the array, and when does it happen?"

    A bounds check. It happens during compilation when the index is already known, and at run time otherwise.

    Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#76-indexing).

??? question "What is the low-level agreement about how values are laid out and passed between functions in machine code?"

    The application binary interface (ABI).

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "What is a straight run of instructions with one way in at the top and one way out at the bottom called?"

    A basic block. Nothing jumps into the middle of it.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What records the calls that have started but not yet finished, adding one on each call and removing one on each return?"

    The call stack.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What is one arrow in a control-flow graph called?"

    An edge. It shows one place execution can go next.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What is it called when an `i32` calculation's true answer does not fit in 32 bits, and what does v0.1 do about it?"

    Integer overflow. Vortex v0.1 reports it as an error and never silently wraps or saturates the value.

    Introduced in [9. Runtime safety](stage-9-runtime-safety.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#runtime-error).

??? question "In a function call, what is the function that makes the call named?"

    The caller. The function being called is the callee.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What is it called when overflow is handled by clamping to the largest or smallest value, and does v0.1 do it?"

    Saturating. Vortex v0.1 does not do it.

    Introduced in [9. Runtime safety](stage-9-runtime-safety.md).

??? question "What do we call a value made of other values, and which v0.1 types are like that?"

    An aggregate. In v0.1 the aggregates are arrays and structs.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What are the unused bytes placed between or after a value's parts, so each part meets its alignment rule, called?"

    Padding.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "Which compiler step turns `[f32; 2 + 2]` into `[f32; 4]` before the program runs?"

    Constant evaluation. Array dimensions are the v0.1 case that needs it.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#72-dimension-rules).

??? question "What do we call a situation where the rules say nothing about what happens next, and can a well-formed v0.1 program reach it?"

    Undefined behavior. Vortex v0.1 does not intentionally expose it to well-formed programs.

    Introduced in [9. Runtime safety](stage-9-runtime-safety.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#15-undefined-behavior).

??? question "What is the full description of a value's size, alignment and the offset of each of its parts called?"

    Its layout.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md). Specification: [8. Structs](../../specification/structs.md#88-layout).

??? question "What do we call the form of the program inside the compiler that is no longer source text but not yet machine code?"

    The intermediate representation (IR). It sits between the front end and the back end.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What do we call a file of machine code that the operating system can start as a program?"

    An executable. The linker produces it from object files and libraries.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What is the value a function hands back to its caller called, and which functions have none?"

    The return value. A `void` function has none.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "When may the compiler leave out a runtime check?"

    Only when the operation is proven safe, known from the source alone to be unable to fail.

    Introduced in [9. Runtime safety](stage-9-runtime-safety.md).

??? question "When testing a runtime check, what do we call the values right at the edge, the last that works and the first that fails?"

    Boundary cases, such as the last valid index and one past it.

    Introduced in [9. Runtime safety](stage-9-runtime-safety.md).

??? question "What is the result of evaluating an expression called, and how many types does it have?"

    A value. Every value has exactly one Vortex type.

    Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What is one call's entry on the call stack, holding its parameters, local variables and return place, called?"

    A stack frame.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What is one basic operation a processor can carry out, such as adding two numbers, called?"

    An instruction. Machine code is a sequence of instructions in numeric form.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which rule says a value must start at an address that is a multiple of some number?"

    Alignment. A four-byte number, for example, is best started at a multiple of four.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "In a control-flow graph, what kind of edge makes a loop?"

    A back edge, one that goes back to an earlier block.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "Which agreement between caller and callee says where arguments are placed and where the return value is found?"

    The calling convention.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "Which instruction moves execution to another block, and what is its unconditional kind often called?"

    A branch. A conditional branch picks between two blocks using a `bool`; an unconditional one is a jump.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What do we call values stored side by side in memory with no gaps?"

    Contiguous. Arrays are intended to use contiguous, predictable storage.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#78-memory-and-layout).

??? question "Which half of the compiler reads the source, works out what it means and rejects bad programs?"

    The front end. In this guide it is stages 1 to 5.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which picture of a function shows basic blocks joined by arrows for where execution can go next?"

    The control-flow graph (CFG).

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What do we call a `return` that ends a function before its last statement?"

    An early return.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "In a function call, what is the function being called named?"

    The callee. It hands its return value back to the caller.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "In `print(width)`, what is this appearance of `width` called, as opposed to the place where it was declared?"

    A use. Name resolution links each use to its declaration.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md).

??? question "What is the large, numbered storage area a running program reads and writes called?"

    Memory, one very long row of bytes, each with its own number.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "What do we say about a declaration whose name can be used at a given point in the program?"

    It is visible at that point. Outside its scope it is not.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md).

??? question "What do we call the block that two or more paths lead into, such as the code after an `if ... else`?"

    A join point.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

??? question "What is the number of a byte in memory called, and which byte gives a value its one?"

    An address. A value's address is the number of its first byte.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "In a value's layout, what is the distance in bytes from the start of the value to one of its parts called?"

    An offset. Each field or element of a value sits at its own offset.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md).

??? question "Scope says where a variable's name is visible; what says how long the variable itself exists while the program runs?"

    Its lifetime. A local variable exists from its declaration until execution leaves its block.

    Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../../specification/statements.md#611-scope-and-lifetime).
